I Am Playing KotOR 2 Using Blasters Only --- This HK Protocol Droid Is My First Obstacle

Part 7 features the blasters squad uniting into one coherent unit, as well as some leveling action - - - all culminating into one final battle against the malevolent HK Protocol Droid. That thing killed all the miners, who could guess that!

What is significant about using blasters only? I mean, if you level your character to be blaster focused, it really shouldn't be that different/harder than if you followed a lightsaber specialization, right? Or is that not the main point of these videos?

Youw ould assume so, but not really. The game is pretty balanced around light sabers, and they are way better than blasters. Theres also not enough loot to go around to all the blaster users, adding additional difficulty. This is definitely KOTOR hardmode

Gotcha gotcha, yeah I just always naturally gravitated toward lightsabers because they're awesome looking and I like pressing Y to twirl them, but I just assumed blasters would be an equal specialization, guess I was wrong.

DungeonMaster explains it pretty well.

While you can spec out a blaster to do similar damage to a lightsaber, the process is much more arduous.

Basically, every lightsaber you get in the game is free. You make your first one from parts you either find our buy for a few hundred credits. Then every lightsaber you get henceforth is either free or a quest reward. And you find most of your decent crystals while traveling throughout the game for no additional cost. There are a few here or there that are costly, but you can get the majority for free.

This is not the case with blasters. Most blasters, simply put, are underwhelming. And when you consider the good blasters, most of them are crazy expensive. Think like 7,000-12,000 credits expensive. And that is for one of them. Good loadouts will use two blaster pistols, so you have to double that investment just to get into the blaster pistol business.

So great! After spending 14,000 credits you have two blasters which will do 4-13 damage, have a 20% chance to stun your opponent, and are fully up-gradable. Meanwhile, a double bladed lightsaber with a couple puny upgrades and some looted crystals could probably do 7-33 damage, as well as augment your force powers (oh yeah, I don't get to use force powers either).

Well, I guess that means I should put some upgrades in my pistols, right? Easy peezy.

Wrong. Good upgrades are crazy expensive as well. Where I am at right now in the game (quite a bit farther than in the linked video), some of these upgrades are costing about 350 components each. There are three components I can put in the blaster pistol, so we'll say that costs about 1,100 components to gear out a blaster pistol... that means I need to scrap whatever look I got into components (and therefore not get credits for more blasters for my other party members).

OK, maybe 1,100 components does not sound too bad (if you are slightly crazy). However, I have a second pistol I need to gear out... so 2,200 components.

And this is only for one character. Not including their armor which I need to purchase and upgrade. Keep in mind, there are nine party members in the game (albeit, you do not have to spec them all out, and three of them are droids).

I'll stop rambling. But the point is, this is quite a bit more challenging than equipping myself and party members with lightsabers --- especially when you consider I cannot use grenades, mines, or force powers either.

Cheers,

Razor Zelkren Teverek
